title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
label: Doc Silver

won.source: Won the vacant title in the three-way final at Vox Hiberionacum, pinning Shawn Hart.

lost.source: Eliminated from the four-way main event of Cherry Blossom Chaos, in which Psycho won the title.

how: Pinned Shawn Hart in the three-way final after Rat Fink held Michael Manson's legs from under the ring.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
label: Psycho

won.source: Won the title by pinning Shawn Hart in the final fall of the four-way main event of Cherry Blossom Chaos.

lost.source: Lost the title to Doc Silver in the steel cage of Rage in the Cage.

how: Pinned Shawn Hart with the Tiger Driver after Doc Silver struck Hart with a steel chair at the Lincoln Memorial.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
label: Doc Silver

won.source: Won the title back from Psycho in the steel cage of Rage in the Cage.

lost.source: Lost the title to Shawn Hart in the Last Man Standing third fall of their best-of-three match at the Spirit of NGEN.

how: Escaped the razor-wire cage, crawling from under the ring after he and Psycho fell through it.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american
label: Michael Manson

won.source: Won the vacant title as the man not pinned in the three-way final at Vox Hiberionacum.

lost.source: Lost the title to Scotty Michaels in a steel cage at the Spirit of NGEN, after Luster's interference.

how: Left unpinned when Doc Silver pinned Shawn Hart in the three-way final; he kept the title through Rat Fink's theft of the belt at Shock & Awe and a three-way ladder match at Cherry Blossom Chaos.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
label: Shawn Hart

won.source: Won the title from Doc Silver, two falls to one, at the Spirit of NGEN.

lost.source: Lost the title to Scotty Michaels in a Winter Wonderland match in Central Park at Merrython.

how: Won the third fall, a Last Man Standing match, on Alex Wylde's ten count after Doc Silver's knee buckled; he had taken the first fall in a lumberjack match after Diablo's fireball blinded Silver. He kept the title against Luster at New World Madness and Michael Manson in a Chicago street fight at Ghoulish Games. He lost it to Scotty Michaels in a Winter Wonderland match in Central Park at Merrython, when Luster, in disguise as Michaels' wheelchair-using brother, laid Michaels across Hart for the pin.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american
label: Scotty Michaels

won.source: Won the title from Michael Manson in a steel cage at the Spirit of NGEN.

lost.source: Lost the title to Richard Gideon in a three-way with Felix Red at Ghoulish Games, passing out in Gideon's figure-four leglock.

how: Pinned Michael Manson with the Viewer's Delight brainbuster after the lights went out and Luster struck Manson with a pipe; he kept the title against Copycat at Almost Live with Luster's brass knuckles.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
label: Diablo

won.source: Handed the title by Shawn Hart on the microphone after Hart won both world titles at the Spirit of NGEN.

lost.source: Lost the title to Rat Fink at NYC Unplugged.

how: Handed the belt by Shawn Hart, who said Diablo had proved himself worthy of defending it by beating Andre Eian in the flaming-tables match.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
label: Rat Fink

won.source: Won the title from Diablo in a falls-count-anywhere match in Central Park.

lost.source: Lost the title to Felix Red at Turkey Day Terror.

how: Pinned Diablo with Falcon's Arrow after The American and Fink Bot joined in; he kept the title against Psycho at Almost Live. He kept the title against Pulsar in a Coal Miner's Glove match at Ghoulish Games.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american
label: Richard Gideon

won.source: Won the title from Scotty Michaels, with Felix Red also in the match, at Ghoulish Games.

lost.source: Lost the title to Psycho in a two out of three falls match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

how: Made Scotty Michaels pass out in the figure-four leglock after Michaels' cousin Shawn Matthews hit his injured leg with a chair; he kept the title against Psycho at Turkey Day Terror when Psycho was disqualified for using a fork. He kept the title in a three-way against Copycat and Psycho at Great Expectations, pinning Psycho with the Buffalo Bomb. He lost the title to Psycho at the Superbowl of Wrestling, two falls to one in a match of submissions only, the Four Corners of Hell and a Texas Death Match.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
label: Felix Red

won.source: Won the title from Rat Fink at Turkey Day Terror.

lost.source: Lost the title to Minion at Great Expectations.

how: Pinned Rat Fink with Ecstasy Through Agony through a table, nineteen minutes in, after two fans, Toxick White and Krist Blue, ran in against Fink's men; he teamed with Richard Gideon as BAD World Heavyweight Champion at Merrython. He kept it against Psycho at Mind Over Matter, when Psycho passed out in his sleeper, and lost it to Minion in a falls-count-anywhere match at Great Expectations.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
label: Scotty Michaels

won.source: Won the title from Shawn Hart in a Winter Wonderland match in Central Park at Merrython.

lost.source: Lost the title to Sean Edmunds in the Ironman match at Great Expectations, five falls to four.

how: Pinned Shawn Hart after Minion had hit him with a chair, the wheelchair-using 'Steve Matthews' had jumped up, hit Hart with the wheelchair and laid Michaels across Hart, the man in the movie mask proving to be Luster; Michaels said the brother and his drunken act were a set-up. The Great Expectations commentary says he also defended the title against Minion and Shawn Hart on a GXW card, Battleground Britain, of which this fed's pages carry no account.
note: The fed's own list of its World Heavyweight champions dates this change to 31 December 2003 and the Edmunds change to 25 February 2004; the first posts of the two broadcasts are dated 30 December 2003 and 18 February 2004, which this record uses.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
label: Sean Edmunds

won.source: Won the title from Scotty Michaels in the Ironman match at Great Expectations, five falls to four.

lost.source: Lost the title to Alex Wylde at Road to Glory.

how: Won the sixty-minute Ironman match five falls to four, the last fall a Northern Lights suplex with seconds left after Luster hit Michaels with a chair and the special referee, Copycat, kicked Michaels; the fed's roleplay pages later have him taken to hospital with a heart arrhythmia.
note: The fed's own list of its World Heavyweight champions dates this change to 25 February 2004 and the Wylde change to 21 March 2004; the first posts of the two broadcasts are dated 18 February 2004 and 10 March 2004, which this record uses.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
label: Alex Wylde

won.source: Won the title from Sean Edmunds at Road to Glory.

lost.source: Lost the title to Michael Manson in a ladder match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

how: Pinned Sean Edmunds with the Gatecrasher superkick after Edmunds, bleeding from the nose, lost his grip on a Northern Lights suplex, the fed's President winning, by the commentary, the first world title of his career; with Pulsar he beat Michael Manson and Rat Fink in a street fight at Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux. He lost it to Michael Manson in a ladder match at the Superbowl of Wrestling, with Joey Melton the special referee.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
label: Minion

won.source: Won the title from Felix Red at Great Expectations.

lost.source: The title was announced vacated at Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux.

how: Pinned Felix Red with the Fall From Grace in a falls-count-anywhere match at Edison Field, after running through an outfield wall and being cut by Felix Red; the line-up announced at Vox Hiberionacum Part Deux says he vacated the title with a torn ligament in his leg.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-world-heavyweight
label: Michael Manson

won.source: Won the title from Alex Wylde in a ladder match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

how: Pulled Alex Wylde off the ladder and took the belt off its hook fifteen feet above the ring, with Joey Melton the special referee; he kept the title against Richard Gideon at BOMB Voyage, the referee calling for the bell at 59 minutes 59 seconds with Gideon in the Tourniquet. He kept the title against Felix Red at Cherry Blossom Chaos II with a clothesline after Red's spinning back kick missed, the referee slow to count in the rain. He kept the title against El Arco Iris at Guerra Interminable, two falls to one under Lucha rules, taking the third fall when Iris tapped to the Tourniquet.
note: The fed's own list of its World Heavyweight champions dates this change to 29 April 2004, the day the post telling the ladder match went up; the first post of the broadcast is dated 18 April 2004, which this record uses.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-north-american
label: Psycho

won.source: Won the title from Richard Gideon in a two out of three falls match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

how: Won two falls to one in a match of submissions only, the Four Corners of Hell and a Texas Death Match, taking the deciding fall when Gideon could not get up at the ten count; Gideon handed him the belt. He kept the title in the Falls Count Anywhere on the Mall II four-way against Rat Fink, Pulsar and El Arco Iris at Cherry Blossom Chaos II and against Golem at Paradise Lost, where he had cut the first referee open with a fork.
note: The fed's own list of its North American champions dates this change to 26 April 2004, the day the post telling the deciding fall went up; the first post of the broadcast is dated 18 April 2004, which this record uses.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
label: Jared Wells

won.source: Won the vacant title in a four-man falls count anywhere elimination match at the Superbowl of Wrestling.

lost.source: Lost the title to Steve Johnson on 17 April 2007, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

how: Pinned Rat Fink with the Alabama Jam from the Heavens, after he had pinned Pulsar and Rat Fink had pinned Felix Red; he kept the title against Mike Lane at BOMB Voyage by pulling him overboard. He kept the title against Iron Lion at Cherry Blossom Chaos II with a Rage Bomb off the second rope after chop-blocking the challenger's knee. He lost it to Steve Johnson on 17 April 2007, with DC Statton refereeing, ending a reign of almost three years, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
label: Steve Johnson

won.source: Won the title from Jared Wells on 17 April 2007, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

lost.source: Lost the title to Jared Wells at Unplugged on 31 December 2009, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

how: Won the title from Jared Wells on 17 April 2007, with DC Statton refereeing, ending Wells's near three-year reign; the fed's own history of the belt gives no finish. He lost it to Wells at Unplugged on 31 December 2009.

title: wfw-worlds-finest-2003-bad-world-heavyweight
label: Jared Wells

won.source: Won the title from Steve Johnson at Unplugged, as the fed's own history of the belt tells it.

how: Beat Steve Johnson at Unplugged on 31 December 2009; the fed's list of 20 January 2010 carried the title and its champion into NGEN.

end.source: The fed's list of its champions of 20 January 2010, served in the NGEN 2010 wing, names Jared Wells the BAD World Heavyweight Champion and says the title would be kept under its name in the fed's relaunch as NGEN, where Wells's reign carries on; this fed's own history of the belt, last edited in May 2010, lists no change after his win at Unplugged.

note: This wing's record of the title ends on 20 January 2010 with Wells still champion; the title and his reign continue in the NGEN 2010 wing.
